requirement: Address QA blocking objections only: make recovery daemon-owned or adopted/tracked, and wire manual stop/archive workflows to durable tombstones.
qa_blocking_objections: Recovery still uses external systemd-run/direct spawn and reports daemon_tracked_restored=0; daemon-owned spawn/adoption remains unresolved.
Tombstone support exists, but manual stop/archive workflows are not wired to create tombstones, so user intent is not durably recorded by normal actions.
constraints: Do not reboot, stop, restart, or kill live services/sessions during implementation or verification.
Do not impose a coarse MemoryMax limit on the whole happy daemon.
acceptance_criteria: Recovery has a daemon-owned spawn/adoption path that makes restored sessions part of daemon tracking, or reports unresolved external state as not restored.
Manual stop/archive paths create durable tombstones that recovery respects.
QA static verification can prove the two blocking objections are resolved without rebooting or killing live sessions.
